screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind randomized trial comparing aminophylline vs placebo in patients with acute ischemic stroke; treatment administered over the initial hospital period consistent with acute timeframe.
Double-blind randomized trial of intravenous aminophylline vs placebo in acute cerebral infarction; intervention given in the acute setting with clinical outcomes reported.
Open-label, single-arm dose-escalation safety study without randomization or a control group; does not meet randomized controlled trial criterion.

Heterogeneous subject group assessing cerebral metabolism; not a randomized controlled trial in acute ischemic stroke patients, and primary intervention is vincamine; aminophylline subgroup not aligned with protocol outcomes/timing.

Randomized cross-over physiologic study in patients recovering from stroke; timing appears subacute rather than within one week and focuses on cerebral blood flow rather than therapeutic clinical outcomes.
Randomized cross-over physiologic study in patients recovering from stroke; timing suggests post-acute phase and examines blood flow metrics, not randomized treatment efficacy within one week.
Small physiologic infusion study assessing cerebral blood flow; not randomized and not a treatment trial in acute ischemic stroke with a control comparator.
Animal study (cats) with middle cerebral artery occlusion; not a human randomized controlled trial.
Animal study in anesthetized dogs comparing cardiovascular effects; not a human randomized controlled trial in acute ischemic stroke.
Mechanistic/clinical experience report noting lack of convincing controlled series; not a randomized controlled trial in acute ischemic stroke within one week.
